notes: Intro call 2025-11-10: AE Liam Chen + SE Maya Patel. AmberWave infra (network + security) + ML platform leads present.
Primary ask: deterministic latency tail for trading assistant. Customer measures client-side p95 (end-to-end) today and ties alerts to that metric.
Requested SLO targets: non-streaming text generation p95 <= 220ms for short completions (<=64 tokens); streaming first-byte p50 <= 120ms, streaming tail p99 <= 700ms.
Measurement ambiguity: client-perceived p95 currently includes mobile websocket and corporate proxy variability. Need canonicalization: server-processing vs end-to-end (network + client).

Redwood proposal: report both server-processing p50/p95/p99 (compute only) and end-to-end p50/p95/p99 (client timestamping). For SLA, canonicalize on end-to-end p95 with specified measurement harness.
SE action: deliver measurement harness (k6 + custom websocket client + synthetic token streamer) and run three load profiles (steady, burst, tail-heavy) with warm/cold KV cache splits.
Throughput / reserved GPU planning: baseline PoC shows need for 12 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs for 99% of peak with model-variant routing (quantized fallback) to avoid SLA breaches during spikes.
Routing & fallbacks: customer requires automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant under burst; Redwood to document throughput vs quality trade-off and rollback policy in SLA.
Security: AmberWave requires SSO/SAML, KMS-backed key rotation (HSM option), audit logs retained 12 months, and quarterly pen-test report before procurement sign-off.
Quote from CTO: "We can't accept token-level variability — our trades rely on consistent tail behavior."
Cost sensitivity: prefers capped committed spend for Dedicated; open to 12-month reserved contract if latency SLOs and throughput guarantees are met.
Next milestone: 2-hour SLO alignment workshop (tech + network + SE) to finalize measurement windows, sampling strategy, and canonical timestamps for SLA reporting.
